title: Stroke-Dysphagia Care-Transition FHIR Implementation Guide
description:
An open, standards-aligned HL7 FHIR R4 Implementation Guide that makes stroke-dysphagia care-transition data computable across the acute, inpatient-rehabilitation, and home/tele-rehabilitation journey, together with a structured terminology-gap analysis (SNOMED CT, LOINC) and an executable decision-support feasibility evaluation in Clinical Quality Language run on a real engine over a synthetic Synthea cohort.

The repository contains six FHIR R4 profiles, six ValueSets (including the two IDDSI axes), a local CodeSystem for instruments that currently lack terminology, an AspirationRiskAlert CQL rule, a conformance harness exercised on two independent servers with negative fixtures, and a fully containerized, seeded evaluation pipeline.

Scope and claims. All data are synthetic or drawn from the published literature. No human or animal subjects, no patient data, and no clinical-benefit or diagnostic claim are involved; the evaluation demonstrates interoperability and computability feasibility, not clinical validity.

Terminology notice. This IG references SNOMED CT, LOINC, and IDDSI codes; it does not redistribute their code systems. The MIT license covers only the source and IG artifacts authored here.
